achievements-bye.where: Achievements: Dex says goodbye and walks off
achievements-bye.text: They’re kept in this browser, for these pages and the desk alike. Now go earn some!

achievements-card.where: Achievements: Dex points at the first badge
achievements-card.text: Each badge says what to do to earn it. Press one to see more, and where to go for it.

achievements-desk.where: Achievements: Dex points at the The 1994 desk heading
achievements-desk.text: The 1994 desk: switch on the PC, dial a BBS, run the programs on it.

achievements-hearts.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Tin heart badge
achievements-hearts.text: Tin hearts are tucked away inside the games. Touch one and it counts here.

achievements-hello.text: Hi! I’m Dex Dynamo, from the year 2000. This page keeps track of everything you’ve done here.

achievements-making.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Making games heading
achievements-making.text: Making games: start one, change a file, run the Level check, download it for DOS or the web.

achievements-playing.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Playing heading
achievements-playing.text: Playing: finish games on the web, on the 1994 desk, even on a phone held sideways.

achievements-reset.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Reset achievements button
achievements-reset.text: Start over forgets the badges in this browser, after asking. Your games and saves stay.

achievements-site.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Around the site heading
achievements-site.text: Around the site: meet the cast, unfold a map, visit the Library. A few badges stay hidden until you find them.

achievements-summary.where: Achievements: Dex points at the count of achievements unlocked
achievements-summary.text: Up top: how many you’ve unlocked so far, out of all of them.

achievements-watching.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Watching heading
achievements-watching.text: Watching: sit back with a walkthrough, or record a video of the screen.

bbs-busy.where: BBS: Dex points at the modem
bbs-busy.text: The PC is busy right now. Quit what’s running, then click the modem to call the BBS yourself.

bbs-bye.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-bye.text: Back to the menu, G says goodbye, and the modem hangs up. NO CARRIER!

bbs-dial.where: BBS: Dex points at the modem
bbs-dial.text: TERMINAL dials 1-412-555-SAND. Hear that screeching? Two modems, shaking hands.

bbs-done.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-done.text: Downloaded and unzipped into C:\DOWNLOAD. When the tour ends, it comes off again, so your drive stays yours.

bbs-download.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-download.text: D and the number downloads it. At 14,400 bits a second, this would take a few minutes.

bbs-hello.text: Dex Dynamo, dialing in from the future! In 1994 you called a BBS: somebody’s own PC, answering the phone.

bbs-login.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-login.text: Connected! It asks for a handle. GUEST gets in without a password.

bbs-logoff.where: BBS: Dex says goodbye and walks off
bbs-logoff.text: That’s a BBS call. The modem on the desk dials one any time you like.

bbs-menu.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-menu.text: The main menu. The letter N scans the newest files: the Sandbox games, free to download.

bbs-ratio.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-ratio.text: Last few callers, then my rule: upload one file for every five you take. Leeches get deleted!

bbs-speed.where: BBS: Dex presses Unlimited in the modem’s speed menu
bbs-speed.text: Too slow? Change the modem’s speed, even mid-call. Unlimited is today’s speed: no waiting!

bbs-sysop.text: And The Sandbox BBS runs right here, on my PC! I’m its SysOp. Go ahead, Dex, give it a call.

bbs-view.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-view.text: V and a file’s number shows its details: what it is, how big, and its author’s notice.

box-back.text: Put the hint book down, and the box comes right back to you.

box-bbs.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the BBS ad in the list
box-bbs.text: An ad for the BBS. Call in and download more.

box-buttons.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the box viewer’s buttons
box-buttons.text: Below, buttons: put the disk in drive A:, read the manual, or close. The arrows pick the next box.

box-bye.where: Box: Inspector Penn says goodbye and walks off
box-bye.text: Case closed. In 1994 a box held disks, a manual, maps, cards, a catalog and stickers!

box-catalog.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the Sandbox Software catalog in the list
box-catalog.text: And the Sandbox Software catalog, with every game in the family.

box-close.where: Box: Inspector Penn presses the box viewer’s Close button
box-close.text: Close, and the box goes back on the shelf, ready for the next curious player.

box-disks.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the disks in the box
box-disks.text: The disks, fanned out as a set. Click them and disk one goes in drive A: to play.

box-hello.text: Inspector Ada Penn, on a new case: what a 1994 software box held. Far more than a disk, as you’ll see.

box-hint-film.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the Red film button
box-hint-film.text: Hint book answers hide in a tangle of lines. Red film lays a red sheet over them, and they show.

box-hint-open.where: Box: Inspector Penn presses the hint book postcard in the list
box-hint-open.text: Stuck? This postcard is about the hint book. Let’s have a look.

box-keycard.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the Key card in the list
box-keycard.text: A key card, a quick reminder of your keyboard.

box-levelmaps.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the Level Maps in the list
box-levelmaps.text: Level Maps show each level’s real map, with the start and the ways out marked.

box-list.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the list of what else came in the box
box-list.text: Then the paper. Each piece has a little picture; click one to look closer. So much, and on purpose!

box-manual.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the manual in the box
box-manual.text: The manual, stapled, with a cover of its own. Click it to read.

box-newsletter.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at The Sandbox Scoop in the list
box-newsletter.text: The Sandbox Scoop, a newsletter about the next games.

box-outside.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the box, turning
box-outside.text: Outside, art up front. The back sells the game with its features, reviews and pictures.

box-postcard.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the Registration card in the list
box-postcard.text: A registration card: a postcard, already marked paid. Handy!

box-shelf.where: Box: Inspector Penn presses the box standing face out
box-shelf.text: Take a box down off the shelf, and the whole thing turns up in your hands.

box-stickers.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the Sticker sheet in the list
box-stickers.text: A sheet of stickers. Cut them out, if you dare.

box-worldmap.where: Box: Inspector Penn points at the World Map in the list
box-worldmap.text: A fold-out World Map: every scene, and the ways between them.

cast-appears.where: Cast: Teddy points at the games Teddy is seen in
cast-appears.text: And the games each one is seen in. Press a picture to go to that game.

cast-bye.where: Cast: Doc Leo says goodbye and walks off
cast-bye.text: Hey, that’s my hat! Thanks for coming to the show, folks.

cast-card.where: Cast: Teddy points at Teddy’s card
cast-card.text: Each regular has a card: who they are, and a little about them. Teddy knows left from right!

cast-families.where: Cast: Teddy points at the three kinds of games
cast-families.text: Three kinds of games: Sandbox Software, the Bard of Bizarre’s songs, and the games from the original CD.

cast-filters.where: Cast: Teddy points at the Show the cast of buttons
cast-filters.text: These show just one kind’s regulars, or everyone.

cast-gwinn.text: It wasn’t me. (It was me.) Zoomies!

cast-hello.text: Smile on: showtime! I’m Doc Leo. This is the cast: everyone from the new games.

cast-next.where: Cast: Teddy presses the Next character button
cast-next.text: The arrows bring on the next one, or the one before.

cast-pick.where: Cast: Teddy points at the Pick a character list
cast-pick.text: Or call one by name from this list.

cast-sound.where: Cast: Teddy points at the stage’s sound button
cast-sound.text: The stage stays quiet until you ask. Then the Teddy games’ theme plays along.

cast-stage.where: Cast: Teddy points at the stage
cast-stage.text: On stage, each regular walks on and says hello, drawn from their own game.

desk-box-disks.where: Desk: Lewie points at the disks in the box
desk-box-disks.text: Inside, the game’s disks. Click them and disk one goes in drive A: to play.

desk-box-extras.where: Desk: Lewie points at the list of what else came in the box
desk-box-extras.text: And everything else that came in the box, each piece ready to read or print.

desk-box-manual.where: Desk: Lewie points at the manual in the box
desk-box-manual.text: Its manual, with a cover all its own.

desk-box-open.where: Desk: Lewie presses the box standing face out
desk-box-open.text: Like this one. Down it comes!

desk-box-turn.where: Desk: Lewie points at the box, turning
desk-box-turn.text: It turns all the way around, so you can read the back. Drag it to turn it yourself, or scroll to zoom.

desk-bye.where: Desk: Lewie says goodbye and walks off
desk-bye.text: That’s my room. Now, who wants to make a game?

desk-clock.where: Desk: Lewie points at the wall clock
desk-clock.text: A giant wristwatch makes a fine wall clock. Turn the lights off and its hands glow.

desk-diskbox.where: Desk: Lewie points at the disk box
desk-diskbox.text: The disk box has a floppy for every game. Pick one and it goes in drive A: and starts.

desk-drive.where: Desk: Lewie points at drive A:
desk-drive.text: That’s drive A:. With a disk in, buttons beside it play it, design it, or open it in today’s web.

desk-enlarge.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Enlarge screen button
desk-enlarge.text: This little button fills the window with the screen. Back to the desk brings the room back.

desk-gmbox.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Game-Maker box
desk-gmbox.text: The Game-Maker box: turn it over, read the Owner’s Guide, or put the CD in and start Game-Maker.

desk-guides.where: Desk: Lewie points at the ? Guides button
desk-guides.text: Press the question mark any time to see this tour again.

desk-hello.text: Hey, I’m Lewie. Welcome to my room! It’s December 1994, and this PC is where the games get made.

desk-keyboard.where: Desk: Lewie points at the keyboard
desk-keyboard.text: Type on your own keyboard, or click the keys here to press them on the PC.

desk-mag-cover.where: Desk: Lewie points at the magazine’s pages
desk-mag-cover.text: The big news on the cover: Game-Maker’s source code, set free!

desk-mag-links.where: Desk: Lewie presses the magazine’s next page arrow
desk-mag-links.text: Its links work, too: they play games, call the BBS, or point out things in my room.

desk-mag-open.where: Desk: Lewie presses the catalog and the magazine
desk-mag-open.text: Let’s peek inside this month’s TURBO BUTTON.

desk-mag-turn.where: Desk: Lewie presses the magazine’s next page arrow
desk-mag-turn.text: Turn the pages with the arrows: reviews, hints, readers’ letters, and ads for the things on this desk.

desk-modem.where: Desk: Lewie points at the modem
desk-modem.text: The modem calls the BBS, where you can download more games. Click its speed to change it.

desk-pad.where: Desk: Lewie points at the game pad
desk-pad.text: The GRAVITAS pad is the PC’s joystick. A real gamepad works too, and a click opens big buttons.

desk-pad-panel.where: Desk: Lewie points at the game pad’s large controls
desk-pad-panel.text: Big buttons for the d-pad’s eight ways and all four buttons. Game-Maker games read the d-pad and the red and yellow buttons.

desk-papers.where: Desk: Lewie points at the catalog and the magazine
desk-papers.text: The shareware catalog and TURBO BUTTON magazine. Read either one; the catalog can even call the BBS.

desk-phone.where: Desk: Lewie points at the wall phone
desk-phone.text: The phone really dials. Try the numbers on Mom’s notes, or call for the time and the weather.

desk-poster.where: Desk: Lewie points at the poster
desk-poster.text: My big plan: shovel snow all winter to buy Game-Maker. Eighty-nine dollars, plus four for shipping!

desk-power.where: Desk: Lewie presses the Power button
desk-power.text: Power switches the PC on. It boots DOS, just like a real one.

desk-screen.where: Desk: Lewie points at the screen
desk-screen.text: Everything runs on this screen: the DOS prompt, Game-Maker, the games, even the BBS.

desk-shelf.where: Desk: Lewie points at the shelf of game boxes
desk-shelf.text: My shelf has a box for every game. Take one down to turn it over, read its manual, or play it.

desk-sticky.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Too retro? sticky note
desk-sticky.text: Too retro? This note takes you to today’s web, with all the same games.

desk-switch.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Desk, DOS and Web switch
desk-switch.text: Desk, DOS and Web switch views. DOS is this same PC, filling the whole window.

desk-turbo.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Turbo button
desk-turbo.text: Turbo runs it at full speed. Switch it off and games crawl along like on an old 286.

dos-bbs.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at BBS in the ⋯ menu
dos-bbs.text: BBS dials the board with the modem. The line speed under it says how fast.

dos-blaster.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at Sound Blaster card in the ⋯ menu
dos-blaster.text: Without the Sound Blaster card, games beep their sounds on the PC speaker.

dos-bye.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks says goodbye and walks off
dos-bye.text: That concludes the tour! Now, if you’ll excuse me, THE CHEZ needs charging.

dos-card.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the registration card
dos-card.text: Or mail the registration card. Once the reply comes, Game-Maker stops asking.

dos-check.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the screen
dos-check.text: Game-Maker may ask for a word from its Owner’s Guide. That was copy protection, back in 1994.

dos-disks.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Disks button
dos-disks.text: Disks is your disk box: Play, Design, or just Insert any game’s floppy in drive A:.

dos-full.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Full screen button
dos-full.text: Full screen hides everything else, the browser too.

dos-gm.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Game-Maker button
dos-gm.text: The Game-Maker button takes you back to it from anywhere, with its CD in drive D:.

dos-guide.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Owner’s Guide beside the screen
dos-guide.text: The guide opens beside it, at the right page, the word marked. Type the word and you’re in.

dos-hello.text: Professor Fiddlesticks, at your service! This is the very same PC, minus the room, filling the window.

dos-keys.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Keys button
dos-keys.text: No keyboard? Keys opens big on-screen keys for the PC.

dos-links.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Links button
dos-links.text: Links lists addresses that open this page on a game, at the prompt, or on the BBS.

dos-manuals.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at Owner’s Guide in the ⋯ menu
dos-manuals.text: The Owner’s Guide is Game-Maker’s manual. The Ultimate Guide has the advanced tips and tricks.

dos-menus.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the screen
dos-menus.text: Then its menus: Play runs a game in PLAYGAME, Design opens the tools that make one, Quit goes to DOS.

dos-power.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Power button
dos-power.text: Power switches it on and off. Off is really off: the next start is a fresh boot.

dos-prompt.text: At the DOS prompt, type GM to come back, or a game’s name on its disk to play it.

dos-reset.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at Reset in the ⋯ menu
dos-reset.text: Reset restarts the PC, like the button on the front of the case.

dos-sound.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Sound button
dos-sound.text: Sound switches the PC’s sound on and off.

dos-switch.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Desk, DOS and Web switch
dos-switch.text: Desk takes you back to the room around this PC, and Web to today’s site.

dos-turbo.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Turbo button
dos-turbo.text: Turbo is sixty-six megahertz of pure speed. Off, it plods along like an old 286.

edit-animation-actions.where: Editor: Lewie points at the frame buttons
edit-animation-actions.text: Duplicate a frame to hold it longer. Move or delete it. Plus Picture adds a GIF after it, from this game or your computer.

edit-animation-bin.where: Editor: Lewie points at the media bin
edit-animation-bin.text: Everything the game has that fits in a show is in the bin. Drag it onto the timeline, or tap it to add it after the chosen slide.

edit-animation-bye.where: Editor: Lewie says goodbye and walks off
edit-animation-bye.text: Pictures that move, shows that play. That is my kind of making. Bye now!

edit-animation-copy.where: Editor: Lewie points at the Copy the area into a block panel
edit-animation-copy.text: The area becomes a block. Pick the block set, see before and after, and press Copy into block. This is how pictures turn into game art.

edit-animation-generate.where: Editor: Lewie points at the Generate button
edit-animation-generate.text: Generate makes an intro, a cast list or a story from the game’s own pictures, characters and text. You can change all of it after.

edit-animation-hello.text: Lewie here. Let me show you how I make things move: animations first, then pictures and slide shows.

edit-animation-picture.where: Editor: Lewie points at the picture
edit-animation-picture.text: A picture. You do not paint it here. Click to choose a twenty by twenty area, and Shift-click snaps to the block grid.

edit-animation-scene.where: Editor: Lewie presses the Scene maker tab
edit-animation-scene.text: The Scene maker. An animation made here keeps its scene, so it opens again just as you left it.

edit-animation-show.where: Editor: Lewie points at the slide show’s timeline
edit-animation-show.text: A slide show is a timeline of pictures, animations and text screens. Drag the edges of a clip to show it longer or shorter.

edit-animation-speed.where: Editor: Lewie points at the speed controls
edit-animation-speed.text: Speed is how long each frame stays, counted in 70ths of a second. Every frame gets the same time. Presets run up to one second.

edit-animation-stage.where: Editor: Lewie points at the animation screen
edit-animation-stage.text: It plays as soon as you open it. The game plays an animation once; Loop here lets you watch it again and again.

edit-animation-strip.where: Editor: Lewie points at the film strip
edit-animation-strip.text: The film strip shows every frame. Click one to see it, or drag it to a new place.

edit-animation-tabs.where: Editor: Lewie points at the Frames and Scene maker tabs
edit-animation-tabs.text: Two ways to work. Frames steps through the pictures one by one. The Scene maker builds the animation from a timeline.

edit-animation-then.where: Editor: Lewie points at the slide’s settings
edit-animation-then.text: Then says what happens after a slide: wait for a key, go straight on, or wait some seconds. From here plays the show from this slide.

edit-animation-timeline.where: Editor: Lewie points at the scene’s timeline
edit-animation-timeline.text: Each track holds items on a timeline: moving text, a walking character, a monster or a block. Drag on the picture to move them.

edit-around-assets.where: Editor: Watt points at the Game assets button
edit-around-assets.text: In the file list, Game assets shows the whole game at once: a card for each kind of file. Press a card to browse those files as pictures.

edit-around-assets-back.where: Editor: Watt points at the Assets button
edit-around-assets-back.text: Back in a file, Assets jumps to that kind’s gallery, so you can try another map or block set.

edit-around-bye.where: Editor: Watt says goodbye and walks off
edit-around-bye.text: Next, the map editor’s tools. Beep!

edit-around-files.where: Editor: Watt points at the list of the game’s files
edit-around-files.text: Files sit in this list by kind, with how many of each. Press a kind’s heading to fold it away or open it again.

edit-around-find.where: Editor: Watt points at the Find a file box
edit-around-find.text: Type part of a name here and the list narrows to match. Handy in a game with a hundred files.

edit-around-guide.where: Editor: Watt points at the Guide link
edit-around-guide.text: And the Guide up here holds the whole manual, whenever you are stuck.

edit-around-hello.text: Beep beep! Watt here again. Let’s find our way around: files, undo, play-testing and help.

edit-around-hint.where: Editor: Watt points at the note about this editor
edit-around-hint.text: Every editor opens with a short note on what it does. On a phone it folds to a line; More opens it.

edit-around-keys.where: Editor: Watt presses the Keyboard shortcuts button
edit-around-keys.text: The keyboard button lists every shortcut: B, L, R and F choose map tools, G shows the grid. The question mark key shows it anywhere.

edit-around-playmenu.where: Editor: Watt presses the arrow beside Play Level
edit-around-playmenu.text: Play-test a level without the title screen. This arrow opens every way the game’s links bring the hero in; pick one to start there.

edit-around-quick.where: Editor: Watt points at the Open a file by name button
edit-around-quick.text: The magnifier opens any file by its name. Ctrl+P does the same, from anywhere in the editor.

edit-around-undo.where: Editor: Watt points at the Undo button
edit-around-undo.text: Undo and Redo step back and forward through your edits in this file. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work too. Nothing to undo here.

edit-around-used.where: Editor: Watt points at the Used by links
edit-around-used.text: Here is every scene that uses this file. Press one to open it in the game’s own scene list.

edit-around-zoom.where: Editor: Watt points at the Zoom list
edit-around-zoom.text: Zoom sets how big the map looks, from 10% to 200%. The mouse wheel zooms around the pointer; Shift and wheel scrolls.

edit-blocks-behave.where: Editor: Joe points at the Walking tab
edit-blocks-behave.text: Walking, Touch and Time set how a block acts: which sides are solid, what touching does, and what it changes into.

edit-blocks-bye.where: Editor: Joe says goodbye and walks off
edit-blocks-bye.text: Quiet, now. Next the monsters, and the hero who meets them.

edit-blocks-colors.where: Editor: Joe points at the palette colors
edit-blocks-colors.text: Click a color to paint with it. Bigger colors, below, shows larger swatches.

edit-blocks-flip.where: Editor: Joe points at the Flip button
edit-blocks-flip.text: Flip and Rotate turn the whole picture. The arrows nudge it a pixel, and Replace colors swaps one color, here or in every block.

edit-blocks-frames.where: Editor: Joe points at the Character frames panel
edit-blocks-frames.text: Character blocks are the hero’s frames. This panel picks an animation and steps through its frames; dashed outlines mark the blocks it uses.

edit-blocks-groups.where: Editor: Joe points at the Groups section
edit-blocks-groups.text: Shift-click or Ctrl-click blocks to pick several. Groups lets you paint them as one big picture.

edit-blocks-hello.text: Joe, the night librarian, speaking softly. Blocks are the little pictures every level is built from. Let’s browse a shelf.

edit-blocks-live.where: Editor: Joe points at the Live character panel
edit-blocks-live.text: Live character plays the animation as you paint, on any background you like, so you see each touch-up in motion.

edit-blocks-mirror.where: Editor: Joe points at the Mirror list
edit-blocks-mirror.text: Mirror repeats each stroke on the other side of the picture, left to right or top to bottom, for tidy symmetry.

edit-blocks-name.where: Editor: Joe points at the block’s name box
edit-blocks-name.text: A name is only for you, so you can tell block 40 is the door. The game never sees it.

edit-blocks-picker.where: Editor: Joe points at the list of blocks
edit-blocks-picker.text: Each file is a set of blocks. Pick one here to edit it. The arrow keys move along the shelf.

edit-blocks-preview.where: Editor: Joe points at the Show with palette button
edit-blocks-preview.text: Show with palette previews the blocks in another palette, such as the night one, before you commit.

edit-blocks-tools.where: Editor: Joe points at the Pencil tool
edit-blocks-tools.text: Pencil, Shade, Fill, Pick color, Line and Box paint the picture. Right-drag erases, and Shade lightens along the palette.

edit-integrator-board.where: Editor: Inspector Penn points at the board of scene cards
edit-integrator-board.text: Each card is a scene, as the player first sees it: the start with its title and menu, every level, and the ending. Drag a card to move it.

edit-integrator-bye.where: Editor: Inspector Penn says goodbye and walks off
edit-integrator-bye.text: Case closed. Every scene is where it should be.

edit-integrator-files.where: Editor: Inspector Penn points at the scene’s files
edit-integrator-files.text: A level’s files: palette, map, block sets, monsters, hero, sounds, music, and the pictures shown before and after it.

edit-integrator-hello.text: A game is a case with many scenes. The Integrator is the board where I pin them all up and see how they connect.

edit-integrator-key.where: Editor: Inspector Penn points at the question mark key
edit-integrator-key.text: The question mark explains the board. The arrows are links: gold ones leave the chosen scene, green ones lead into it.

edit-integrator-links.where: Editor: Inspector Penn points at the links table
edit-integrator-links.text: Links are the exits. Each goes to another scene, from a block on this map to a block on the next. Point one at the winning ending and the game is won.

edit-integrator-music.where: Editor: Inspector Penn presses the Music tab
edit-integrator-music.text: Music lists each scene’s song, with a play button when its file is in the game.

edit-integrator-player.where: Editor: Inspector Penn points at the DOS player button
edit-integrator-player.text: And this button opens the DOS player, the program that runs the game on a real computer. That is the last stop.

edit-integrator-scene.where: Editor: Inspector Penn points at the chosen scene’s panel
edit-integrator-scene.text: Click a card to work on that scene. Rename it here, play from it, make its level card, or delete it.

edit-integrator-screens.where: Editor: Inspector Penn presses the Screens tab
edit-integrator-screens.text: Screens lists every title, menu and between-level picture. Click one to jump to the scene that uses it.

edit-integrator-tools.where: Editor: Inspector Penn points at the board’s tools
edit-integrator-tools.text: Add level scene starts a new level beside the last. Auto-arrange tidies the cards. PNG saves a picture of the whole board.

edit-integrator-zoom.where: Editor: Inspector Penn points at the zoom buttons
edit-integrator-zoom.text: Zoom in and out, or Fit to see every scene. Scroll or pinch works too, and the arrow keys step from one scene to the next.

edit-map-blocks.where: Editor: Dex points at the Blocks tab
edit-map-blocks.text: The side column has tabs. Blocks is the list of background blocks to paint with; Monsters lists the creatures to place.

edit-map-bye.where: Editor: Dex says goodbye and walks off
edit-map-bye.text: Now go make something big. Next up, the block editors!

edit-map-exits.where: Editor: Dex points at an exit marker
edit-map-exits.text: With Links on, gold arrows are exits to other scenes. Drag one to move it, or click it to see where it leads.

edit-map-find.where: Editor: Dex points at the Find button
edit-map-find.text: Find lights up every use of the chosen block on the map. Replace, beside it, swaps one block for another everywhere.

edit-map-grid.where: Editor: Dex points at the Grid button
edit-map-grid.text: Grid draws lines between the blocks, so you can count them. The G key switches it on and off.

edit-map-hello.text: Dex Dynamo here! Let’s get into the map editor and work through its tools, one by one.

edit-map-options.where: Editor: Dex points at the Tool options tab
edit-map-options.text: Tool options shows the settings of whichever tool you chose: shapes, terrains, stamps and buildings.

edit-map-paint.where: Editor: Dex points at the Paint tool
edit-map-paint.text: Paint, Line, Rectangle and Fill lay down the chosen block; keys B, L, R and F pick them. Pick is an eyedropper: it takes a block from the map.

edit-map-select.where: Editor: Dex presses the Select tool
edit-map-select.text: Select drags out a rectangle or a polygon. Then fill it, copy, cut and paste it, or save it as a stamp or a block group.

edit-map-stamp.where: Editor: Dex points at the Stamp tool
edit-map-stamp.text: A stamp is a saved patch of blocks, a house or a tree. Place it where you like, flipped or turned. Select makes new ones.

edit-map-terrain.where: Editor: Dex points at the Terrain tool
edit-map-terrain.text: Terrain is for grass, water or paths. Make one from blocks you have: a fill, edges and corners. Then dragging picks the right piece for you.

edit-map-ways-in.where: Editor: Dex points at a way-in marker
edit-map-ways-in.text: Cyan marks are ways in: where the hero arrives. A number means several arrive at one spot; press it for the list.

edit-map-wrap.where: Editor: Dex points at the Wrap button
edit-map-wrap.text: Wrap shows the map repeated all around. Scroll through an edge and the opposite side follows.

edit-monsters-anim.where: Editor: Max points at the Animation panel
edit-monsters-anim.text: A monster is a few frames, each a picture and a time in ticks, a tick being an eighteenth of a second. Add or remove frames here.

edit-monsters-birth.where: Editor: Max points at the frames of the move
edit-monsters-birth.text: A frame can show the hero, or give birth to a monster. Preview monsters from picks which set shows up here.

edit-monsters-bye.where: Editor: Max says goodbye and walks off
edit-monsters-bye.text: Delivery complete. Next stop: the colors!

edit-monsters-hello.text: Courier Max here, with a special delivery: the monsters first, then the hero who meets them.

edit-monsters-hero.where: Editor: Max points at the At the start tab
edit-monsters-hero.text: Now the hero. The first tab is how the game starts: hit points, lives, money, five counters and the starting inventory.

edit-monsters-list.where: Editor: Max points at the list of monsters
edit-monsters-list.text: Every monster in the set, numbered. Pick one, and the rest of the page shows how it looks and acts.

edit-monsters-move.where: Editor: Max points at the Movement list
edit-monsters-move.text: Movement: it follows its path, chases the hero, runs away from it, or wanders at random.

edit-monsters-moves.where: Editor: Max points at the list of sequences
edit-monsters-moves.text: Your own moves follow, each started by a key or a joystick direction. The function keys stay with the game’s own menus.

edit-monsters-path.where: Editor: Max points at the path map
edit-monsters-path.text: The path is drawn on a real map: Map picks the scene, Starts at the monster’s spot. Click blocks to lay corners; it walks to each in turn.

edit-monsters-pick.where: Editor: Max presses monster 52 in the list
edit-monsters-pick.text: This one, number 52, follows a path of seven corners. Let’s see where it walks.

edit-monsters-power.where: Editor: Max points at the Power box
edit-monsters-power.text: Power is how tough it is: 100 or more can’t be killed by touching the hero. The Lives box says how long it lasts, forever or until destroyed.

edit-monsters-seqs.where: Editor: Max presses the Sequences tab
edit-monsters-seqs.text: Sequences are the hero’s moves. The built-in ones come first: Idle, Die, Hurt, Pick up and Drop.

edit-monsters-stage.where: Editor: Max points at the audition stage
edit-monsters-stage.text: The stage auditions the move. Pause, Restart and Sound off are under it, and Behind picks which scene it plays in.

edit-monsters-tabs.where: Editor: Max points at the sequence’s tabs
edit-monsters-tabs.text: Four tabs per move: Controls says what starts it, Animation how it moves, Requirements what it needs, Sound what plays.

edit-palette-backgrounds.where: Editor: Watt presses the Backgrounds tab
edit-palette-backgrounds.text: Backgrounds previews the game’s own screens, drawn on color 0: high scores, status, help and about.

edit-palette-bye.where: Editor: Watt says goodbye and walks off
edit-palette-bye.text: That is the editor, top to bottom. Happy making! Beep.

edit-palette-hello.text: Beep beep! This is the palette: all 256 colors a DOS game can show at once.

edit-palette-picker.where: Editor: Watt presses the big color swatch
edit-palette-picker.text: The big swatch opens a picker with hue, saturation and brightness, a friendlier way to find a color.

edit-palette-ramp.where: Editor: Watt points at the Spread range button
edit-palette-ramp.text: Spread range blends the colors between your two ends. Make a shade ramp turns a range into shades of the first color.

edit-palette-reduce.where: Editor: Watt presses the Copy button for colors from a picture
edit-palette-reduce.text: Copy brings colors in from a picture, shrunk to fit. Pick a range first, and it reduces the picture to that many.

edit-palette-reduced.where: Editor: Watt points at the Colors from picture box
edit-palette-reduced.text: Colors are chosen from the pixels the picture really uses, the common ones first. Nothing lands until you press the Apply colors button.

edit-palette-reserved.where: Editor: Watt points at the Reserved color ranges section
edit-palette-reserved.text: Reserve ranges for characters, monsters or backgrounds, so one kind never takes another’s colors. Only the editor keeps this.

edit-palette-rgb.where: Editor: Watt points at the red box
edit-palette-rgb.text: Red, green and blue each run from 0 to 63, like a real VGA card. Slide them or type a number.

edit-palette-square.where: Editor: Watt points at the color picker
edit-palette-square.text: Drag in the square, or use the arrow keys. Nothing changes until you press Confirm color; Cancel keeps things as they were.

edit-palette-swatches.where: Editor: Watt points at the palette’s colors
edit-palette-swatches.text: Click a color to edit it. Shift-click a second one to pick a whole range.

edit-palette-tabs.where: Editor: Watt points at the Color tab
edit-palette-tabs.text: Three tabs. Color edits the one you chose. Vision and Backgrounds check how the palette looks in play.

edit-palette-variants.where: Editor: Watt points at the Night, dusk, underwater section
edit-palette-variants.text: Night, dusk, underwater: versions of this palette for other times of day. Glowing colors keep lamps and stars bright.

edit-palette-vision.where: Editor: Watt presses the Vision tab
edit-palette-vision.text: Vision shows a level as players who see color differently would, and lists colors that look alike.

edit-player-bye.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks says goodbye and walks off
edit-player-bye.text: Splendid! A player of your own design. Now go and make something wonderful!

edit-player-colors.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks presses the Colors tab
edit-player-colors.text: Colors are shared by every screen. Each is a color picker, and the number beside it is the VGA level, out of 63.

edit-player-files.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks presses the Files tab
edit-player-files.text: Files changes the three-letter endings of the files in the DOS download, and the program is patched to look for them.

edit-player-hello.text: Ah, my favorite invention yet: the player itself! Its words, colors and frames may be tinkered with, though not to bursting.

edit-player-hiscores.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks presses the High scores tab
edit-player-hiscores.text: Every tab lists its screen’s changes by kind. High scores has words, positions, colors and how long it waits.

edit-player-intro.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the box’s introduction
edit-player-intro.text: The player’s own words, colors, frames and timings can change, screen by screen. This game is look-only, so every box is locked.

edit-player-nudge.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Move controls
edit-player-nudge.text: Prefer keys? Choose a word under Move, then press the arrows to nudge it a pixel. Hold Shift to move eight.

edit-player-open.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks presses the DOS player button
edit-player-open.text: This button opens the DOS player. That is the program the DOS download uses to run a game outside the editor.

edit-player-presets.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the presets
edit-player-presets.text: Presets are two classic tricks: blank the menu words, or rename the status words. Reset all puts everything back.

edit-player-preview.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the preview screen
edit-player-preview.text: The preview is drawn with your changes. Drag a word or a frame to move it, or a frame’s corner to resize it.

edit-player-tabs.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the screen tabs
edit-player-tabs.text: One tab for each screen, in the order a player meets them: menu, text pages, high scores, status, save, load, help. Then keys, colors and files.

edit-player-words.where: Editor: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the first section of words
edit-player-words.text: Words come first. Each line has to fit the room it has in the program, and takes plain letters, digits and punctuation.

edit-sounds-accompany.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the Accompany button
edit-sounds-accompany.text: The Accompany button writes bass, chords and drums around a track’s tune. Copy tune makes a faster, slower or higher copy as a new song.

edit-sounds-change.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the Change it buttons
edit-sounds-change.text: Change it reshapes what you have: higher, lower, faster, reversed, echo, vibrato. Silence clears every step. Undo is at the top.

edit-sounds-columns.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the PC and SB columns
edit-sounds-columns.text: Two columns of play buttons. PC is the little speaker in the case. SB is a Sound Blaster, which plays a recording when there is one.

edit-sounds-hello.text: Woof! My favorite editor: sounds first, then music. Everything a game can make you hear.

edit-sounds-inst.where: Editor: Gwinn presses the Instruments tab
edit-sounds-inst.text: Instruments are the FM sounds of the Sound Blaster’s chip. Shape one with sliders and waves, then press Try it to hear a note.

edit-sounds-list.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the list of sound effects
edit-sounds-list.text: Thirty effects, numbered. The game plays the first nine by itself. The rest wait for a character’s move to ask for them.

edit-sounds-make.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the Make one buttons
edit-sounds-make.text: Make one composes a new effect: coin, jump, laser, explosion. Each press is a different one, and it plays at once.

edit-sounds-music.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the list of tracks
edit-sounds-music.text: Now music. A song is a handful of tracks, one line of notes each. Every track has its own instrument, and you can mute or solo it.

edit-sounds-pitch.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the pitch bars
edit-sounds-pitch.text: The speaker sound is drawn: thirty-six bars of pitch, each a bit over a hundredth of a second. Drag across to draw, to the bottom for silence.

edit-sounds-play.where: Editor: Gwinn presses the Play as the game would button
edit-sounds-play.text: Play as the game would: the recording on a Sound Blaster if it comes with one, the speaker sound if not.

edit-sounds-play-song.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the Play button
edit-sounds-play-song.text: Play starts from the cursor, and Space does the same. Click the ruler to choose a start, or drag along it to mark a loop.

edit-sounds-roll.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the music tools
edit-sounds-roll.text: Notes go on the piano roll. The pencil draws, the box selects, the eraser rubs out and the hand moves you around.

edit-sounds-settings.where: Editor: Gwinn presses the Settings tab
edit-sounds-settings.text: Settings: the drum kit, the song’s speed, where it repeats, and how loud it is. Then you are done. Woof!

edit-sounds-voc.where: Editor: Gwinn points at the Sound Blaster sample chooser
edit-sounds-voc.text: Pick a recording for this effect here, a voc file. Leave it on PC speaker only and every computer plays the speaker sound.

editor-assistant.where: Editor: Watt points at the Assistant button
editor-assistant.text: The Assistant lets your own AI look at a game and change it with you. Set it up in Settings first.

editor-blocks.where: Editor: Watt points at the Blocks list
editor-blocks.text: Pick a block from this list…

editor-building.where: Editor: Watt points at the Building tool
editor-building.text: Building drags out a whole house, any size, from its parts.

editor-bye.where: Editor: Watt says goodbye and walks off
editor-bye.text: Time to recharge. Happy making! Beep.

editor-check.where: Editor: Watt points at the Level check panel
editor-check.text: The Level check lets a bot play the level, then shows where it went and what players might mind.

editor-copy.where: Editor: Watt points at the Edit a copy button
editor-copy.text: Ready to make it yours? Edit a copy, and start changing things.

editor-files.where: Editor: Watt points at the list of the game’s files
editor-files.text: Every file in the game, sorted by kind: palettes, blocks, monsters, maps, music and more.

editor-hello.text: Beep! Watt here, from Ohm Sweet Ohm. This is the editor, open on my game just as it shipped.

editor-level.where: Editor: Watt points at the Play Level button
editor-level.text: Play Level jumps straight into a level. The arrow beside it picks which one, and where to start.

editor-links.where: Editor: Watt points at the Links button
editor-links.text: Links shows the doors: gold marks are exits to other scenes, cyan marks are where the hero comes in.

editor-map.where: Editor: Watt points at the map’s name
editor-map.text: This is a map: one level, laid out in blocks, a hundred by a hundred.

editor-monsters.where: Editor: Watt points at the Monsters tool
editor-monsters.text: Monsters puts the game’s creatures on the map. A right-click takes one away.

editor-paint.where: Editor: Watt points at the Paint tool
editor-paint.text: …then paint with it. Line, Rectangle and Fill lay down lots at once.

editor-palette.where: Editor: Watt points at the note about color 0
editor-palette.text: In a palette, mind color 0: the game draws its menus and text screens on it. Press backgrounds to see them.

editor-play.where: Editor: Watt points at the Play Game button
editor-play.text: Play Game plays it from its title screen, right here, without leaving the editor.

editor-readonly.where: Editor: Watt points at the Read-only bar
editor-readonly.text: Looking inside changes nothing. Edit a copy makes your own copy of the game to change.

editor-terrain.where: Editor: Watt points at the Terrain tool
editor-terrain.text: Terrain paints grass, water or paths, and chooses the edges and corners for you.

guide-bye.where: Guide: Inspector Penn says goodbye and walks off
guide-bye.text: Case closed. When you’re stuck, the answer is usually in here.

guide-contents.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at The editors in the Guide’s contents
guide-contents.text: The contents, one part at a time. The editors explains each tool, from maps to music.

guide-hello.text: Inspector Ada Penn. Every case needs a good guide, and so does making games. This is it.

guide-home.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at The home page heading
guide-home.text: Here, the home page: making a new game, bringing one in, and every shelf of games.

guide-next.where: Guide: Inspector Penn presses the next part’s link
guide-next.text: At the bottom, the next part’s name takes you on. One clue at a time.

guide-owners.where: Guide: Inspector Penn presses the Open the Owner’s Guide button
guide-owners.text: The Owner’s Guide explains every part of a game, and how the parts fit together.

guide-owners-page.where: Guide: Inspector Penn presses the Owner’s Guide’s next page arrow
guide-owners-page.text: It opens in the Game-Maker box, as it came in 1994. Turn the pages, or print it as a booklet.

guide-sharing.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at Sharing your game in the Guide’s contents
guide-sharing.text: Sharing your game: a web app for any web host, a copy for real DOS, or just its files.

guide-start.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at the Getting started heading
guide-start.text: Getting started: how to design, play and share games in this web version.

guide-tip.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at the tip for new game makers
guide-tip.text: New here? Play a game, Look inside it, Edit a copy, then change one small thing and play again.

guide-ultimate.where: Guide: Inspector Penn presses the Open The Ultimate Owner’s Guide button
guide-ultimate.text: The Ultimate Owner’s Guide is about making a game people enjoy. The Level check uses its checklists.

guide-ultimate-read.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at The Ultimate Owner’s Guide, open
guide-ultimate-read.text: Heroes that feel right, levels that teach, fair enemies, then play-testing. A case file for every game.

home-achievements.where: Home: Teddy points at Achievements in the header
home-achievements.text: Achievements keeps track of what you’ve done, here and on the 1994 desk.

home-another.where: Home: Teddy presses the Another button
home-another.text: Another picks a different game at random. Ooh, good one.

home-bye.where: Home: Gwinn says goodbye and walks off
home-bye.text: That’s the tour! Now go play something.

home-cast.where: Home: Teddy points at Cast in the header
home-cast.text: The Cast page is where you meet Teddy, me, and everyone else from the new games.

home-download.where: Home: Teddy points at the Download button
home-download.text: Download makes a copy to play on Windows, a Mac, Linux, the web, or real DOS.

home-games.where: Home: Teddy points at Games in the header
home-games.text: Games, up in the bar, always brings you back here.

home-guide.where: Home: Teddy points at Guide in the header
home-guide.text: The Guide explains making games, one part at a time.

home-guides.where: Home: Teddy points at the ? Guides button
home-guides.text: Press this button any time to see this tour again, or to have Teddy and me wait on a page for you.

home-hello.text: Hi! I’m Gwinn. This little guy is my brother Teddy. He and I will show you around.

home-imported-none.where: Home: Teddy points at the import tile
home-imported-none.text: Nothing here yet? Drop game files on this tile, or click it to pick them.

home-library.where: Home: Teddy points at Library in the header
home-library.text: The Library has things to read and print: manuals, maps, sticker sheets and a magazine.

home-look.where: Home: Teddy points at the Look inside button
home-look.text: Look inside opens its files in the editor, just as they shipped. Change something and you get a copy of your own.

home-new.where: Home: Teddy presses the New game button
home-new.text: New game starts one of your own: ready to play, empty, or described in words for your own AI to build.

home-note.where: Home: Teddy points at the Add a note button
home-note.text: Add a note keeps a few words about a game, just for you.

home-notes-search.where: Home: Teddy points at the Find a game box
home-notes-search.text: And the search box finds the words in your notes, too.

home-offline.where: Home: Teddy points at Play offline in the Settings menu
home-offline.text: Settings has Play offline, which saves the whole site so it works with no connection.

home-play.where: Home: Teddy presses the Play button
home-play.text: Play starts it right here in your browser, with the keyboard or a gamepad.

home-rate.where: Home: Teddy points at the rating stars of the imported game up top
home-rate.text: Up top is one of them. Give it one to five stars: your rating saves at once.

home-search.where: Home: Teddy points at the Find a game box
home-search.text: Looking for one game? Type part of its name here.

home-shareware-notice.where: Home: Teddy points at the shareware games
home-shareware-notice.text: They’re other people’s games, so most just play here, exactly as released. Each keeps its author’s notice.

home-shareware-what.where: Home: Teddy points at the shareware games
home-shareware-what.text: Shareware meant try it free. If you kept playing, you sent the author a fee. Games got around on floppy disks and BBSes.

home-show.where: Home: Teddy points at the Show rating picker
home-show.text: Show narrows the list to one rating, or to the games you haven’t rated yet.

home-showcase.where: Home: Teddy points at the big game picture at the top
home-showcase.text: Up top is one game, shown big. Its picture plays a short demo of the game.

home-sort.where: Home: Teddy points at the Sort by picker
home-sort.text: Sort by Rating puts your five-star games first, with the unrated ones last.

home-stars.where: Home: Teddy points at a rated tile’s stars
home-stars.text: Rated games wear their stars on their tiles.

home-tab-bizarre.where: Home: Teddy presses the Bizarre tab
home-tab-bizarre.text: Bizarre: big, heartfelt songs about all the wrong things, each one made into a game.

home-tab-gameware.where: Home: Teddy presses the Gameware tab
home-tab-gameware.text: Gameware: the free games that came with Game-Maker. Play one, or edit a copy to see how it works.

home-tab-imported.where: Home: Teddy presses the Imported tab
home-tab-imported.text: Imported holds games you bring in: a folder, some files, a .zip, or a one-page export.

home-tab-mine.where: Home: Teddy presses the My games tab
home-tab-mine.text: My games: the ones you make here, or copy from a shelf to change. They stay in this browser.

home-tab-sandbox.where: Home: Teddy presses the Sandbox tab
home-tab-sandbox.text: Sandbox: new games made with Game-Maker in its original formats, so they play in real DOS too.

home-tab-shareware.where: Home: Teddy presses the Shareware tab
home-tab-shareware.text: Shareware: games other people made with Game-Maker, from the CD and the BBSes.

home-tabs.where: Home: Teddy points at the collection tabs
home-tabs.text: These tabs are the collections: your games, ones you bring in, and shelves of games ready to play.

home-theme.where: Home: Teddy points at Theme in the Settings menu
home-theme.text: Theme switches between dark, light, or whatever your computer uses.

home-tiles.where: Home: Teddy presses a game tile
home-tiles.text: Pick any tile and its game moves up top.

home-views.where: Home: Teddy points at the Desk, DOS and Web switch
home-views.text: Desk, DOS and Web: a 1994 desk with its PC, DOS Game-Maker on its own, or this page.

home-walkthrough.where: Home: Teddy points at the Walkthrough button
home-walkthrough.text: Walkthrough plays the whole game for you, or lets the bot make one, and you can play parts of it yourself.

library-all.where: Library: Lewie presses the All games button
library-all.text: Showing just one game? This puts everything back on the shelves.

library-bye.where: Library: Joe says goodbye and walks off
library-bye.text: Please return every word to its book. Exactly one hundred at a time.

library-card.where: Library: Lewie points at the first manual on the shelves
library-card.text: Each card opens its piece on screen: a manual, a hint book, a map, a key card. Most can be printed, too.

library-count.where: Library: Joe points at the count of things on the shelves
library-count.text: This counts everything on the shelves. I counted them too. Twice.

library-guide.where: Library: Lewie points at the Guide card
library-guide.text: The Guide and the help for Mac, Windows and Linux are shelved here as well.

library-hello.text: Good evening. I’m Joe, the night librarian. Everything on these shelves is to read, print or watch.

library-lewie.text: Hi, I’m Lewie! I shoveled a lot of snow to buy Game-Maker. All the paper from the game boxes is here.

library-magazine.where: Library: Lewie points at the TURBO BUTTON card
library-magazine.text: TURBO BUTTON is the shareware gamer’s monthly: news, reviews, hints and every game.

library-pick.where: Library: Lewie points at the Game or Kind picker
library-pick.text: Pick one game, or one kind, to see just that shelf.

library-print.where: Library: Lewie points at a Disk labels card
library-print.text: Disk labels and retail boxes open in the print shop, with lines to cut and fold along.

library-sort.where: Library: Lewie points at the By game and By type buttons
library-sort.text: Sort the shelves by game, or by type: every manual together, every map together.

library-walkthrough.where: Library: Lewie points at a Walkthrough card
library-walkthrough.text: Every game’s walkthrough is here too, played start to finish. Its length is on the card.

settings-ai.where: Settings: Max points at AI setup in the Settings menu
settings-ai.text: AI setup connects your own AI, on your computer or with your own key, for the editor’s Assistant.

settings-backup.where: Settings: Max points at Back up / restore in the Settings menu
settings-backup.text: Back up saves everything this browser keeps to one file. Restore brings it back, here or on another computer.

settings-bye.where: Settings: Max says goodbye and walks off
settings-bye.text: Delivered. Signed, sealed, and on to the next world.

settings-credits.where: Settings: Max points at Credits in the Settings menu
settings-credits.text: Credits names who and what made everything here. That’s this page.

settings-hello.text: Courier Max, with a delivery: the settings. They live behind the gear, top right.

settings-offline.where: Settings: Max points at Play offline in the Settings menu
settings-offline.text: Play offline says how big the whole site is, then saves it all, so it works with no connection.

settings-page.where: Settings: Max points at the Credits page’s sections
settings-page.text: This page’s sections: the people who made the original Game-Maker, the game authors, and every tool used, AI too.

settings-source.where: Settings: Max points at Source on GitHub in the Settings menu
settings-source.text: Source on GitHub: every line of this site’s code, open for anyone to read.

settings-theme.where: Settings: Max points at Theme in the Settings menu
settings-theme.text: Theme goes dark, light, or whatever your computer uses. Each press picks the next one.

settings-tour.where: Settings: Max points at Guided tour in the Settings menu
settings-tour.text: Guided tour plays this whole tour again, every page in order.
